events.text:
## Recommendation
- **Go to South Haven first** for the pier. I'd expect it to be about average (2 of 4), with St. Joseph a close second.
- **Grand Haven is also about average (2)**, and it's the only pier with a recent good result, but that was in late August.
- **Muskegon is the weakest bet (1 of 4)**, since its pier has been slow in every recent report.
- Start with glow spoons or live bait near the pierheads. Those are what worked from piers in the last few weeks.

## Why
- The pier reports from the last four weeks were slow at all three ports that had them, and the anglers blamed warm water (Muskegon and Grand Haven, 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-02).
- I'd expect the cooling near South Haven and St. Joseph to help the pier most, because the satellite water there dropped about 9 F in the last 3 days, the largest drop of the four ports (conditions summary for the week before today).
- I'd expect Muskegon to stay weakest because its near-pier water was still the warmest of the four in the same summary, at about 67 F.

## Evidence
**Recent reports** (newest is 2026-09-09, 13 days old)
- Grand Haven, 2026-09-09: pier "slow", "No salmon were reported from the pier by anglers casting spoons."
- Muskegon, 2026-09-09: pier "slow", "Pier anglers were unsuccessful targeting salmon due to warm water temperatures."
- Grand Haven, 2026-09-02: pier "very slow action due to increased water temperatures."
- Muskegon, 2026-09-02: pier "slow fishing due to warmer water conditions."
- Grand Haven, 2026-08-26: pier rated good (3). "Salmon were caught from the pierheads in 70 feet of water," on glow spoons, glow plugs, white flies, and live bait.
- Muskegon, 2026-08-26: one Chinook from the pier on glow spoons, rated below average (1).
- St. Joseph and South Haven had no pier entries in these reports. Their boat reports were average (St. Joseph, 2026-09-09, best bite about 120 ft) and below average (South Haven, 2026-09-09).

**Past seasons**
- I did not run the past-season comparison. The conditions tool did not return live water, so I had no current surface temperature to match against history.

**Conditions** (the tool returned a summary for the week before 2026-09-22, not live data)
- South Haven: satellite water averaged 63 F and fell 9 F in the last 3 days. Upwelling-favorable wind blew 44 hours in those 3 days and 66 hours over the week.
- St. Joseph: satellite water averaged 62 F and fell 9 F in the last 3 days. Upwelling wind blew 33 hours in the last 3 days and 47 hours over the week.
- Grand Haven: satellite water averaged 66 F and fell 2 F in the last 3 days, with 47 upwelling hours in the last 3 days.
- Muskegon: satellite water averaged 67 F and fell 2 F in the last 3 days, with 52 upwelling hours in the last 3 days.
- The DNR's preferred range for Chinook and coho is 52–58 F (general guidance, NY DEC), so all four ports were still above it.

## Caveats
- **Report age:** the newest DNR report is from 2026-09-09, 13 days old. The pier ratings are my expectations for this week, not reports of it.
- **Conditions are not live:** the conditions tool said live data was unavailable and returned the week before today. Check the current buoy and pierhead temperatures before you go.
- **Gaps:** South Haven and St. Joseph had no recent pier reports, so their ratings rest on the cooling and the boat reports.
- **Wind:** a strong north-to-east wind would push warm water offshore and help the pier bite, but it would also make the lake rough for anyone on the pier.

## Sources
- Sept 9 bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/4292fc6
- Sept 2 bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/4280cb4
- Aug 26 bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/426de2b
